title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 139
paragraphs: After the Pelasgians had killed their own sons and wives, the earth no longer bore fruit for them, nor did their women or their livestock bring forth young as they had before. Hard pressed by famine and barrenness, they sent to Delphi to ask for a release from the troubles that lay upon them; and the Pythia told them to pay whatever penalty the Athenians themselves should set. So the Pelasgians came to Athens and said they were willing to make amends for all the wrong they had done. The Athenians laid a couch in the most splendid style in the City Hall, and setting beside it a table covered with every good thing, they ordered the Pelasgians to hand over their land in that same condition. The Pelasgians answered: “When a ship shall accomplish the voyage from your country to ours in a single day with a north wind behind it, then we will hand it over” — confident that this was impossible, since Attica lies far south of Lemnos.
